To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Bispyridinium compounds, which have been identified as potential treatments for organophosphorus nerve agent poisoning, are potent antagonists of both muscle and neuronal nicontinic receptors; (2) The potency of these compounds as antagonists depends on the length and flexibility of the linker between the two positively charged pyridinium moeties; (3) This knowledge will help to optimise these molecules as therapeutic agents against the nicotinice effects of poisoning.

the bispyridinium compound with a ten-carbon linker between the two quaternary nitrogen atoms has the highest inhibitory potency for both neuronal and muscle-type nicotinic acetycholine receptors, as well as for acetylcholinestrase, and therefore has the most potential for therapeutic use against organophosphorus-induced nicotinic effects.
